newsitem.title: THAILAND: Stocks unfazed as Thai bank delays limits.
newsitem.headline: Stocks unfazed as Thai bank delays limits.

text.p: Thai bank stocks were little moved by the central bank's postponement on Thursday of measures aimed at limiting the amount of foreign loans that their offshore units could bring in for re-lending locally.
But bankers welcomed the postponement, saying that if the measures had been implemented, they would have significantly affected their loan portfolios.
"It's good news. If the measures were implemented they would have significantly affected our lending plan for the rest of the year," said a senior banker at Nakornthon Bank.
When the Bank of Thailand (BOT) guidelines were first circulated to financial institutions earlier this month, bank stocks were sold off on fears that such measures could limit their earnings growth.
Bank stocks prices also fell sharply at that time because foreign funds were also underweighting their portfolios in Thailand and moving to other regional markets, brokers said.
A senior BOT official told Reuters that the measures, due to be in effect from September to December, were postponed after banks had made representations to the central bank on the matter.

The central bank also needed more time to collate the relevant data to come up with a plan for the future, said Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, director of the BOT's financial institutions supervision and developement department.
The measures if they had been implemented would have raised the minimum on offshore loans raised for relending by banks to US$5 million from $2 million.
Any rise in offshore loans extended during September-December this year would have been limited to seven percent of the increase of baht-denominated loans they lend out over the same period.
Bank stocks firmed slightly but brokers said it was more due to a technical rebound and bargain-hunting by locals at cheap prices.
At around 0755 GMT, Bangkok Bank Plc was up two baht to 187 and Krung Thai Bank Plc up one at 70 baht per share.

"It is good news for the money market and will help keep liquidity high. But there is not much reaction from the stock market because it is viewed more as a matter for financial institutions than as an equities matter," said Thanadech Mahapokai, first assistant vice president at Book Club Finance and Securities Plc.
Pattera Dilokrungthirapop of Crosby Research said the postponement news was positive for bank stocks as they could help banks' earnings grow.
"But people are cautious about banks because of worries about asset quality," she added.
